On the flip side, there were still enough people to pop on Private servers to maintain sustainable populations in the long term.

I think this is why Blizzard opted for adapting Layering technology early on: They're likely anticipating a massive population surge early on, so if the populations recede, they can disable it, whereas if the populations remain high, they can just start adding servers.

I'm sure there will be plenty of people trying it out of curiosity (doubly-so since the sub is tied to Retail), but I'm guessing it will definitely become its own "thing", for lack of better term.

The first is for them to make Burning Crusade/Wrath of the Lich King legacy servers, since both of those are in pretty high demand. The second is for them to sort of do an "alternative timeline", where they make new content for Classic. I'd presume the style of the content would be more "in-line" with the "spirit" of Classic, but only time would tell on that one. I could see something along the lines of content that ended up being cut from Classic, like fleshing out some quest lines that were never completed, or adding more content to barren zones, e.g. Azshara.

But something tells me that the best WoW fans can hope for is a faithful recreation of vanilla and Blizzard not fucking-up somehow.
